Lesson Title: Lesson 1: Band II Core Words — Technology
Message (What to Teach): Technology vocabulary is essential for Module C unseen texts. Learn 10 key tech words.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Matching: Match the word to its definition. device / innovate / digital / access / download

Lesson Title: Lesson 2: Band II Core Words — Environment
Message (What to Teach): Environmental topics appear frequently. Master these 10 words.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Fill in the blank: "We need to ______ the environment by using less plastic." (protect / pollute / ignore)

Message (What to Teach): Connectors make your writing flow. Learn "first of all," "second of all," "in my opinion," "for example," "to sum up."
Exercise Type / Snippet: Sentence completion: "______, I believe childhood is the most important time." (In my opinion / However / Therefore)

Lesson Title: Lesson 4: Band II Core Words — Education
Message (What to Teach): Education is a common Module C theme.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Word bank exercise: "We all ______ at home and at school." (learn / teach / study)

Lesson Title: Lesson 5: Band II Core Words — Health & Lifestyle
Message (What to Teach): Health and lifestyle vocabulary appears in unseen texts.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Multiple choice: Which word means "to deal with a problem"? A) ignore B) cope with C) avoid

Message (What to Teach): Words have different meanings in different contexts. Learn to infer meaning.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Context clues: "The residents of the small town were worried." What does "residents" mean?

Message (What to Teach): Spaced repetition solidifies memory. Review all 40 words from Lessons 1-6.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Quizlet Live: 20-question vocabulary race against classmates.

Message (What to Teach): Expand your word bank with more Band II Core II words.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Create sentences: Write 5 original sentences using new vocabulary words.

Lesson Title: Lesson 9: Skimming for the Main Idea
Message (What to Teach): Don't read every word. Skim to understand the general topic in 30 seconds.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Skim practice: Read the passage quickly (30 sec). What is the main idea? A) Technology B) Education C) Environment

Message (What to Teach): Read the questions first, then scan for keywords in the text.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Scan practice: "Find the word 'extinction' in the text. What sentence is it in?"

Lesson Title: Lesson 11: Differentiating Main Ideas & Supporting Details
Message (What to Teach): The 2020 curriculum expects students to differentiate between main ideas and supporting details.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Categorization: Sort these sentences into "Main Idea" or "Supporting Detail."

Lesson Title: Lesson 12: Answering "According to the Text" Questions
Message (What to Teach): The answer is always in the text. Find it, don't guess.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Text-dependent question: "According to the text, why is childhood important?" (Answer must quote or paraphrase the text)

Message (What to Teach): Three wrong answers, one right. Learn to spot distractors.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Distractor identification: "Which of these is NOT mentioned in the text?"

Message (What to Teach): Some answers aren't stated directly—you need to "read between the lines."
Exercise Type / Snippet: Inference practice: "The author says 'many people were worried.' What can you infer?"

Message (What to Teach): Use context to guess unknown words.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Context clues exercise: "The traditional customs of the tribe were passed down for generations." What does "customs" mean?

Message (What to Teach): Apply all skills to one complete unseen text.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Full practice: Read the text and answer 5 comprehension questions.

Message (What to Teach): Texts have structure: introduction, body, conclusion. Identify each part.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Structure labeling: Label each paragraph as Intro, Body, or Conclusion.

Message (What to Teach): Why did the author write this? To inform? Persuade? Entertain?
Exercise Type / Snippet: Purpose identification: "The author's main purpose is to..." (inform / persuade / entertain)

Message (What to Teach): Detect the author's attitude—positive, negative, or neutral.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Tone detection: "The author's attitude toward the topic is..." (positive / negative / neutral)

Message (What to Teach): Module C may ask you to compare ideas from two passages.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Comparison exercise: "How are Text A and Text B similar? How are they different?"

Message (What to Teach): Summarize a text in your own words.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Summary writing: "Write a 3-sentence summary of the passage."

Message (What to Teach): You have limited time. Practice answering questions quickly.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Timed practice: 5 questions in 10 minutes.

Message (What to Teach): Don't panic. Use strategies to understand challenging texts.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Strategy practice: Read a difficult text. Circle words you don't know. Guess their meaning from context.

Message (What to Teach): Apply all strategies to a full unseen text.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Full practice + self-assessment: Answer questions, then check answers with a partner.

Message (What to Teach): Opinion essays follow a formula: Introduction → Reasons → Conclusion.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Structure labeling: "Label the parts of this opinion essay: Introduction, Reason 1, Reason 2, Conclusion."

Message (What to Teach): Start with "I would like to tell you why I think..." or "In my opinion..."
Exercise Type / Snippet: Introduction writing: "Write an introduction for: 'Why is it important to learn English?'"

Message (What to Teach): Use "First of all," "Second of all," "For example" to build your argument.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Sentence expansion: "Add a connector to this sentence: '______, children learn to talk.'"

Message (What to Teach): End with "To sum up" and restate your opinion.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Conclusion writing: "Write a conclusion for the childhood opinion essay."

Message (What to Teach): Describe a person you admire. Include appearance, personality, and why you admire them.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Descriptive paragraph: "Describe a person you admire. Write 5-7 sentences."

Message (What to Teach): Describe a place or experience using sensory details.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Descriptive paragraph: "Describe your favorite place. Use at least 3 sensory details."

Message (What to Teach): Adjectives make descriptions vivid. Learn to use them.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Adjective upgrade: "Replace the weak adjectives with stronger ones: 'good' → '______', 'big' → '______'."

Message (What to Teach): Write a complete opinion essay on a given topic.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Full essay: "Write an opinion essay: 'Should schools teach students to protect the environment?'"

Lesson Title: Lesson 33: Letter Format — Formal vs. Informal
Message (What to Teach): Know the difference between formal and semi-formal letters.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Format identification: "Is this letter formal or informal? Why?"

Message (What to Teach): Learn appropriate openings ("Dear Sir/Madam") and closings ("Yours faithfully," "Yours sincerely").
Exercise Type / Snippet: Fill in the blank: "______, I am writing to complain about..."

Message (What to Teach): Structure a complaint letter: problem → details → requested action.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Letter writing: "Write a letter of complaint about a product you bought."

Message (What to Teach): Structure a request letter: introduction → request → reason → thanks.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Letter writing: "Write a letter requesting information about a summer course."

Message (What to Teach): Compare opinion essays, descriptions, and letters.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Type identification: "Read these three texts. Which is an opinion essay? A description? A letter?"

Message (What to Teach): Learn to give and receive constructive feedback.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Peer review: "Swap essays with a partner. Use the checklist to give feedback."

Message (What to Teach): Use a checklist to catch common mistakes before submitting.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Self-edit: "Use the checklist to review your own essay. Fix 3 things."

Message (What to Teach): Write any type of composition on a given prompt.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Choice essay: "Choose one: opinion essay, description, or letter. Write 100-150 words."

Message (What to Teach): Simulate the real Module C exam experience.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Full exam: "Read the unseen text and answer 5 questions. Then write a paragraph on the given topic."

Message (What to Teach): Review the reading section in detail. Learn from mistakes.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Error analysis: "Why did you get Question 3 wrong? What strategy could you have used?"

Message (What to Teach): Review the writing section. Identify strengths and areas for improvement.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Writing improvement: "Rewrite your paragraph using the feedback."

Message (What to Teach): Rapid-fire vocabulary review.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Speed quiz: "Define these 20 words in 2 minutes."

Message (What to Teach): Review all reading and writing strategies.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Strategy sorting: "Match each strategy to the skill it helps (skimming, scanning, inference, etc.)."

Message (What to Teach): Second full simulation to build stamina.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Full exam #2: Another unseen text + writing task.

Message (What to Teach): Focus on each student's personal weak spots.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Personalized practice: "Based on your past exams, practice these 3 question types."

Message (What to Teach): You are ready. Believe in yourself.
Exercise Type / Snippet: Motivation: "Write down 3 things you are good at in English. Share with a partner."
